blocks.summary: Plants turn light, water and carbon dioxide into sugar and oxygen, in two stages inside the chloroplast.

sections.heading: Stage 1: light reactions
paragraphs: In the thylakoid membranes, chlorophyll absorbs light and splits water. Oxygen is released, and the energy is stored in two carriers, ATP and NADPH.

sections.heading: Stage 2: the Calvin cycle
paragraphs: In the stroma, the plant uses that ATP and NADPH to fix carbon dioxide into a three-carbon sugar. Six turns of the cycle make one glucose.
